chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abil Jawza' al-Munabbih ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no monasticism, nor tourism (or wandering for devotion), nor silence (fasting of speech) in my nation,' meaning silence.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things not found in the Muslim nation according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the Prophetic rejection of ascetic withdrawal, specifically defining 'samt' as silence or inaction rather than mere quietude. This reflects the Shia emphasis on active engagement in worldly affairs and governance as part of worship, contrasting with the Christian monastic tradition of *rabbaniyyah* and the pre-Islamic practice of *siyahah* (devotional wandering). The narration underscores that true Islamic piety involves dynamic participation in society rather than isolation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-154 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Abil Jo’aza al-Monabat ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Alvan, on the authority of Amr ibn Khalid, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (MGB)
that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “There is no monastism; tourism, and (fast of) silence in my nation.”
